For a large-scale industrial project in the 
Port of Antwerp, we are looking for an experienced 
Electrical & Instrumentation (E&I) Inspector.
 

You will join an international project environment within the petrochemical industry, where 
English is the main working language. Your focus will be on ensuring that all electrical and instrumentation works are executed safely, correctly and in accordance with project specifications, applicable standards and approved documentation.
 

Your role
 

As an E&I Inspector, you will be closely involved in the construction, installation and pre-commissioning phases of the project. You will spend a significant amount of time in the field, following up contractors and verifying the quality and compliance of the E&I installations.
 

Your responsibilities will include:
 
 

• Inspecting electrical and instrumentation installations during construction and completion 

• Verifying installations against approved drawings, specifications, datasheets and relevant standards 

• Checking cable routing, cable trays, cable pulling and termination 

• Inspecting junction boxes, field instruments, panels, switchgear and other E&I equipment 

• Checking instrument installation, impulse tubing and associated hook-ups 

• Verifying grounding, bonding and earthing installations 

• Performing and witnessing electrical and instrumentation tests 

• Following up loop checks, continuity tests, insulation resistance tests and functional testing 

• Verifying installations in hazardous areas and checking compliance with 
ATEX requirements 

• Reviewing inspection and test records, punch lists and construction documentation 

• Identifying non-conformities and following up corrective actions with contractors 

• Supporting mechanical completion and pre-commissioning activities 

• Coordinating closely with construction, engineering, QA/QC and commissioning teams 
 

• A technical degree or equivalent experience in Electrical Engineering, Instrumentation, Automation or a related discipline 

• Several years of experience as an 
E&I Inspector, QA/QC Inspector or E&I Supervisor in an industrial environment 

• Experience within 
petrochemical, chemical, oil & gas or other process industries 

• Strong knowledge of electrical and instrumentation installation practices 

• Experience with 
ATEX / hazardous area installations 

• Familiarity with relevant IEC standards and industrial E&I practices 

• Experience with inspection procedures, ITPs, punch listing and quality documentation 

• The ability to read and interpret 
single-line diagrams, wiring diagrams, loop diagrams, hook-ups, P&IDs and technical datasheets 

• A strong focus on safety, quality and technical compliance 

• Good communication skills and the confidence to address contractors when installations do not meet the required standards 

• A professional working proficiency in 
English

Are you a hands-on technical professional who enjoys taking ownership, solving practical challenges, and creating a safe, efficient, and well-organized working environment? Do you like working independently, improving processes, and supporting technicians and colleagues by ensuring the right facilities, tools, and equipment are available when needed?
 

Then this could be your next career move
 

To strengthen our team in 
Antwerp, we are looking for a proactive and reliable 
Facility & Toolshop Coordinator who will take ownership of our facility operations and Toolshop management. In this independent and hands-on role, you will be responsible for maintaining a professional, safe, and efficient working environment across our office and workshop facilities. You will combine technical skills, organizational ability, and a strong sense of ownership to ensure that our employees have the right workplace and tools to perform their activities successfully.
 

This is not a traditional facility role. As Facility & Toolshop Coordinator, you will be the process owner of our Toolshop and the key contact for facility-related activities within Everllence Belgium. Your contribution directly supports our workshop teams, field service engineers, and daily operations. If you are someone who sees what needs to be done, takes initiative, and enjoys making improvements happen, we would like to hear from you. 

What makes this role unique?
 

You will have responsibility for two important operational areas: 
Facility Management and Toolshop Management.
 

You will ensure that our workplace remains safe, organized, and operational while also managing the complete lifecycle of our professional tools. From registration and availability to inspection, maintenance, and return processes, you ensure that every tool is traceable, safe, and ready for use. You will work closely with workshop technicians, field service engineers, HSE, Procurement, and external suppliers. Your role is essential in creating operational reliability and supporting our teams to deliver high-quality service to our customers.
 

Your role
Facility & Workplace Management
 
 

• Take ownership of facility operations, including office, workshop, storage areas, and workplace improvements. 

• Perform and coordinate maintenance activities, repairs, and technical improvements. 

• Ensure a safe, clean, and professional working environment. 

• Manage facility services, suppliers, and maintenance partners. 

• Support safety, compliance, logistics, and workshop organization.  

Toolshop Management
 
 

• Own and coordinate the daily Toolshop process, including tool availability, registration, and traceability. 

• Ensure tools are maintained, inspected, calibrated, and safely available for technicians. 

• Manage tool inventory, repairs, replacements, and preparation of equipment for projects. 

• Support workshop and field service teams by providing the right tools at the right time. 

Who are you?
You are a hands-on and reliable professional with a strong sense of ownership. You enjoy solving practical challenges, working independently, and creating a safe and organized working environment.
 

You bring:
 
 

• A proactive and solution-oriented mindset. 

• Strong technical understanding and practical skills. 

• A structured, accurate, and safety-focused way of working. 

• Good communication skills and a service-oriented attitude.   

Your experience & qualifications
 
 

• Technical or facility-related background with experience in an industrial environment. 

• Basic mechanical and electrical knowledge. 

• Experience with maintenance, tools, inventory, or facility processes. 

• Experience with digital systems and administration. 

• Valid driving license B. 

• VCA certification or willingness to obtain one. 

• Experience within the maritime sector, tool management, inspections, or Lean/5S is an advantage. 

• Languages: Dutch fluent and good professional English.

• Real autonomy and the opportunity to quickly progress towards a Head of Sales roleHow to Apply

jobs.occupation: AI Implementation Intern with specific focus on AI adoption in European HR M/W/X
jobs.description:
This internship offers a unique opportunity to explore how Artificial Intelligence can enhance HR, Recruitment, Learning & Development, and other people-related functions by identifying opportunities for process optimisation, automation, and improved employee experience.

 

• Analyse business processes across People & Culture, Human Resources, Talent Acquisition, Learning & Development, and related people functions to identify opportunities for AI adoption and process optimisation.
• Research AI tools, technologies and emerging solutions applicable to people-related business processes.
• Evaluate existing workflows and identify opportunities for automation, improved efficiency and enhanced employee experience.
• Benchmark industry best practices and AI use cases across HR and People functions.
• Develop recommendations for AI implementation, including suitable technologies, expected business impact and implementation considerations.
• Assess organisational readiness, transformation anticipated risks, required capabilities and change management considerations for AI adoption.
• Collaborate with HR, People and Culture Director and business stakeholders to validate opportunities and prioritise initiatives.
• Present findings, business cases and implementation roadmaps to project stakeholders. 
• Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's programme in Human Resources, Business, Psychology, AI, Computer Science, Data Science, ICT Management, Information Systems, or a related field.
• Strong interest in the practical application of Artificial Intelligence within business functions, particularly HR, Recruitment, and People Operations.
• Good understanding of current AI technologies, including generative AI, automation, workflow optimisation, or intelligent process improvement.
• Analytical mindset with the ability to map business processes and identify opportunities for increased efficiency.
• Excellent research and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate findings into practical recommendations.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
• Knowledge of German, French and/or Dutch is considered a strong advantage.
• Previous exposure to AI tools (e.g. Claude, Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Microsoft Power Platform, automation platforms, or similar technologies) is an asset.
• Candidates with a combination of HR knowledge and AI/technology expertise are particularly encouraged to apply.

 What will you do?
